Documentation

01 / Setup & preferences

Getting started

Start with a photo or video. Match the camera first, then set the floor and scale before adding objects or characters.

Install and prepare

WHERE Blender → Edit → Preferences → Add-ons

Perspectra runs in Blender 4.2 or later on Windows, macOS and Linux. Install the add-on ZIP first, then download the Python packages and models for the tools you plan to use.

  1. Choose Install from Disk in Blender’s add-on preferences, select the Perspectra ZIP, and enable the add-on.
  2. Open Perspectra’s preferences. Check System and Compute, then install the required Python packages shown there. Restart Blender if an installation asks you to.
  3. In the 3D Viewport, press N and open the Perspectra tab. Choose Photo or Video and a quality mode. Download the models offered for that workflow.
  4. Run Test Installed Models in preferences. Once the required models are available, start your first estimate or track.
i

This manual covers the current full development build.

Fast, Normal and Best#

WHERE Photo or Video → quality buttons

Start with Normal. Try Fast to check a shot before a longer run, or Best if you need a more detailed estimate and have time and memory to spare. The preset also affects object masks.

i

Compare the alignment against the original footage before keeping a slower preset. Photo and Video can require different model downloads.

Switch sources without losing your place#

WHERE Photo → Image / Video → source field

You can switch between references in the same .blend file. Choose a different image or clip and Perspectra hides the previous result; choose the original source to bring it back. Running Estimate or Re-track again replaces the solve for that source.

i

Save the .blend and keep its external media and Perspectra cache available. A saved scene does not make every external analysis file part of the .blend.

02 / Setup & preferences

Preferences

Preferences apply to this computer. Set how much memory Perspectra workers can use, choose a CPU or GPU, install models, and decide where to store tracking data. For an individual shot, choose Photo or Video and set the quality in the Perspectra sidebar.

Open and save Perspectra preferences#

WHERE Blender → Edit → Preferences → Add-ons → Perspectra

Start here on a new computer. This is where you install what Perspectra needs and check that it can run before opening a shot.

  1. Open Edit → Preferences, select Add-ons, and search the add-on list for Perspectra. Enable it if necessary, then expand its entry.
  2. Check Memory, System and Compute. Install the required Python packages, then download the models needed for your chosen workflow.
  3. Run Test Installed Models and check the Cache folder status before processing a long clip.
  4. Blender normally saves preferences automatically. If Auto-Save Preferences is disabled in its preferences menu, click Save Preferences to keep your changes. See Blender’s preference-saving instructions.
i

If the model list and cache settings are missing, install the required Python packages first. Those controls appear after installation.

Worker Memory Budget (GiB)#

WHERE Preferences → Memory

Perspectra’s background jobs and their child processes share one memory budget. The default is 8 GiB. Raising the value allows those workers to use more memory. Changes apply to new runs. Set the value to 0 to disable the budget.

Lower the budget to leave more memory available for Blender and other apps. This can help keep your computer responsive while tracking. A lower limit can also make tracking take longer because the worker may need to retry a solve and process overlapping frames more than once.

  1. Video tracking chooses how many frames to buffer and how many FFmpeg threads can decode the source. Larger source frames use more memory per thread. Other active Perspectra jobs reduce the budget available to the tracker.
  2. For example, on a 12-core computer with the full budget available, a 2160 × 4096 clip can start with 6 decoder threads at 4 GiB or 12 threads at 8 GiB.
  3. If a batch exceeds the budget during a full video track, Perspectra keeps completed batches and retries the unfinished frames with fewer decoder threads or smaller overlapping batches as needed. If the clip fits in one batch, Perspectra keeps a continuous camera solve and runs each lens candidate in a fresh worker. Smaller retry batches can also queue lens candidates this way. When joining batches, Perspectra checks that their camera positions and rotations agree on shared frames.

For example, a six-second shot of a man loading packages onto a dolly had 152 frames at 24 fps. With Track Every Frame off, Normal sampled 76 frames. Solving all 76 together exceeded the 8 GiB worker budget, so the tracker retried with a limit of 38 sampled frames per batch and joined three overlapping batches into one camera track.

i

Perspectra samples worker memory periodically, so brief peaks can exceed the setting. Blender’s own memory, other applications and dedicated GPU memory are outside this budget.

System and Compute#

WHERE Preferences → System and Python packages

Perspectra detects your operating system and picks an initial Compute setting. System controls which packages appear in the list; Compute chooses the CPU or GPU for supported models. Some models always run on the CPU.

  1. Keep System set to the operating system of this computer. Selecting a different system only changes the displayed requirements; its packages cannot be installed here.
  2. Choose the Compute setting for your hardware from the table below.
  3. Install any newly required packages and models, restart Blender if prompted, and use Test Installed Models before starting another job.
System and Compute controls
CONTROL WHAT IT DOES
macOS → GPU Uses Metal on supported Apple hardware when the model supports it. If you select NVIDIA CUDA on macOS, Perspectra uses this setting instead.
Windows → GPU Uses DirectML with compatible DirectX 12 GPUs, including supported NVIDIA, AMD and Intel hardware.
Windows or Linux → NVIDIA CUDA Use with a supported NVIDIA GPU. Requires the additional CUDA runtime packages offered in the list; the ONNX Runtime CUDA download is approximately 2 GB.
Linux → GPU On Linux, GPU runs models on the CPU. Choose NVIDIA CUDA if you have a supported NVIDIA card and want to use it.
CPU Runs models on the CPU. Try this if your GPU is unsupported or a job fails with GPU acceleration. Processing usually takes longer.
i

Compute sets where models run. To change the quality, choose Fast, Normal or Best in the Photo or Video sidebar. GPU support depends on the model, hardware, drivers and installed packages.

Install Python packages#

WHERE Preferences → System and Python packages → package rows

Install the packages marked as required for your System and Compute settings. Each row shows the licence, approximate download size, and either the installed version or an install button. Check the list again if you switch from CPU to GPU.

  1. Install each missing required package using its row’s button. Add optional packages when the workflow you plan to use needs them.
  2. Follow the shared progress bar at the top of this section. Let the current operation finish before starting another installation; use Cancel if you need to stop it.
  3. Read any installation error shown there. If Blender reports Restart Blender to finish installing, save your work and restart before testing.
  4. Use the refresh icon to re-check package status, then continue with model downloads.
i

If a package is marked not available, check which operating system and Compute setting it needs. Changing the System menu won’t make a Windows package run on a Mac, for example.

Download AI models#

WHERE Preferences → AI models → Photo / Video / People tracking / Object tracking

Before working offline, download the models for the tools and quality presets you plan to use. The list shows what each model is for, its licence and size, and whether it’s installed. Perspectra picks the model when you choose a workflow and preset.

  1. Choose the workflow and quality you intend to use in the sidebar. In preferences, find models whose Used in column includes that mode, or follow the workflow’s download prompt.
  2. Click a missing model’s size/download button. Watch progress under System and Python packages; a partial-size label lets you resume an interrupted model download.
  3. If a row reports a file problem, click Repair download. After the files are ready, run Test Installed Models.
Download and repair AI models controls
CONTROL WHAT IT DOES
Model / Used in Identifies the model and the modes or optional tools that need it. Shared models may serve several workflows.
Licence Shows the model or asset licence separately from the add-on licence. Review the relevant terms for the intended use.
Size / checkmark A download button means files are missing or incomplete. A checkmark and size mean the files are present; use the setup test to check that they load.
Download All Downloads all missing or damaged models for the selected System and Compute settings. Check the total download size first, especially if you’re preparing several tools for offline use.
Folder Shows where downloaded models are stored. The Cache folder setting below controls tracking data, not this model folder.
i

Initial setup and downloads require network access. Processing uses local files after the requirements are available. Optional models and people controls depend on the installed build.

Test Installed Models and refresh#

WHERE Preferences → System and Python packages → Test Installed Models / refresh icon

Click Test Installed Models if a download looks complete but a tool still won’t start. It checks whether the installed packages and models can run. The refresh icon just updates the list of installed files.

  1. Finish package installation, model downloads and any requested Blender restart.
  2. Click Test Installed Models and wait for Testing… to finish.
  3. Read the result below the button. A failure names the affected package or model and gives a reason. Correct that issue, then test again.
  4. Use the adjacent refresh icon after completing an installation or repair when the displayed status needs updating.
i

The test checks installed components. A passing result does not mean every optional model has been downloaded, and it does not measure camera-tracking accuracy on your footage.

Choose the Cache folder#

WHERE Preferences → Cache folder

Choose a writable folder for new tracking runs. A long clip can take several gigabytes, so pick a drive with room to spare. Leave the field blank to use the default folder in Perspectra’s add-on data.

  1. Choose a writable folder on a drive with sufficient free space, or clear the field to return to the default location.
  2. Read the status beneath the field. It reports the resolved location and free space, or a write/access problem. The current implementation warns when less than 2 GB is free.
  3. Use a new tracking run to write to the selected location. Keep previous result files available when reopening existing scenes.
i

Changing this preference does not migrate every existing project cache. A scene remembers the folder its track used, while new runs use the current preference. Avoid temporary folders for results you need to keep. Model downloads have a separate location.

Clear Analysis Cache#

WHERE Preferences → trash icon beside Cache folder

The trash icon clears reusable analysis for all videos, including data Perspectra finds in older cache locations. Blender asks you to confirm before it clears anything.

  1. Finish active tracking work before clearing its reusable data.
  2. Click the trash icon beside Cache folder and confirm Clear Analysis Cache if you want to clear analysis across videos.
  3. Expect the next track to recompute the removed analysis. To clean only the current clip’s heavy cache, use Video → Free Cache instead.
i

This clears analysis data, not installed AI models or the separate saved track-result files. Free Cache in the Video sidebar has a narrower, current-clip scope.

03 / Photo

Match a camera to a photo

A single image can suggest lens, orientation and scale, but it does not uniquely describe a 3D scene. Let the estimate give you a starting point, then check it against visible edges and known dimensions.

Estimate Camera#

WHERE Photo → choose an Image → Estimate Camera

Choose a photo and run Estimate Camera. Perspectra creates a Blender camera with the photo as its background. It estimates the field of view, orientation, lens distortion, camera height and scene scale, then adds guides so you can fine-tune the match.

  1. Choose the reference image and a quality preset.
  2. Click Estimate Camera and wait for the job to finish.
  3. Inspect the camera view. Check long edges, verticals and the horizon; adjust guide lines if needed.
  4. Set the floor, verify scale with a known measurement, and place a Test Cube before building detailed geometry.
i

Frontal views, parallel edges, cropped images and scenes with little structure can leave the lens or horizon uncertain. Read the warning on the photo and supply a known lens or better guide lines.

Focal length and FOV#

WHERE Photo → Camera

If you know the lens used for the photo, enter its focal length or horizontal field of view (FOV). Both controls change the same framing: a wider angle shows more of the scene; a longer lens shows less.

Focal length and FOV controls
CONTROL WHAT IT DOES
Focal length A millimetre value tied to the camera’s sensor width. Physical focal length and 35 mm-equivalent focal length are not interchangeable without accounting for the sensor.
FOV Horizontal field of view in degrees. Useful when you know the actual image angle of view, or the reference has already been cropped.
Live Update / Update Live Update applies edits as you make them. Turn it off to make several changes, then use Update.
i

Changing focal length changes perspective matching; changing scene scale changes distances. Use the lens to fix framing geometry, then use scale to fix real-world size.

Correct with Guide Lines#

WHERE Photo → Camera → Correct with Guide Lines

Find two sets of edges that meet at a right angle in the scene, such as the seams in a tiled floor. Line up each pair of guides with edges that are parallel in real life. Perspectra uses where they converge in the photo to adjust the lens and camera angle.

  1. Place the two lines of one colour along two parallel edges in one world direction.
  2. Place the other pair along parallel edges in the perpendicular world direction. Use long, clearly visible edges rather than shadows or curved outlines.
  3. Hold Tab to inspect the floor grid and horizon. Adjust handles while checking the whole image.
  4. Press Enter or C, or choose Finish Guide Lines, to keep the result. Esc or right-click cancels the active guide edit.
i

The two colour families must describe perpendicular real-world directions. Merely choosing two unrelated sets of parallel lines can produce a convincing but incorrect camera.

Read the AI Lines overlay#

WHERE Photo → Camera → Advanced → AI Lines

Turn on the detected lines to see what the camera estimate followed. Red, green and blue mark the X, Y and Z directions. If the horizon looks tilted, check whether those lines follow fixed edges such as walls or shelves.

Read the AI Lines overlay controls
CONTROL WHAT IT DOES
Used Show lines assigned to a vanishing-point family.
All Show used lines, outliers and rejected candidates.
Rejected Inspect lines the solve discarded.
Extend Draw extensions towards the vanishing points to reveal convergence.
Opacity Reduce the overlay so you can still inspect the image beneath it.
i

AI Lines shows what Perspectra detected. To correct the camera match yourself, adjust the Guide Lines.

04 / Photo

Lens and perspective

A tilted camera, a shifted lens and a distorted image can look similar near the centre but behave very differently at the edges. Choose the correction that matches how the picture was made.

Auto, Level + shift and Tilted#

WHERE Photo → Camera → Advanced → Perspective

Auto estimates the perspective from the photo. You can override it by looking at vertical edges, such as the sides of a building.

Matching verticals

If the sides of a building stay parallel, choose Level + shift. It keeps the camera level and shifts the framing. If they narrow toward the roof because the camera looked up, choose Tilted.

Auto, Level + shift and Tilted controls
CONTROL WHAT IT DOES
Align to Lines Use the detected scene axes for camera orientation. Switch it off when those detected directions do not represent the structure you want to match.
Warning on Photo Shows uncertainty or disagreement in the camera estimate directly on the reference. Hide it only after you have read and addressed it.

Original photo and Undistorted#

WHERE Photo → Camera → Lens distortion detected

Original photo keeps the image as shot and bends the guides and grid to match the lens. Undistorted straightens the background so you can line up geometry with a regular perspective camera. The difference is easiest to see near the edges of a wide-angle photo.

i

An overlay bending correctly over the original photo does not mean ordinary solid-view geometry is also lens-distorted. Use the Undistorted background for a straight-camera comparison, or Lens Preview for the original-lens view.

Correct lens bend by hand#

WHERE Photo → Original photo → Guide Lines

If a guide touches both ends of a straight wall but bows away in the middle, drag its middle handle until it follows the wall. Confirm the edit to rebuild the corrected background.

  1. Use the Original photo background and open Guide Lines.
  2. Lay the guide along an edge you know is straight, such as a door frame. Drag the middle dot until the guide follows the curve in the photo.
  3. Check several edges before confirming. Use Reset Lens Distortion to return to the measured bend if the manual correction is worse.
i

Pick an edge that was straight before the photo was taken. A bent pipe, a curved wall or wobble from a rolling shutter can lead you to apply too much lens correction.

Lens Preview#

WHERE Photo → Camera → Lens Preview

Render a preview through the photo’s lens to see how your model lines up with the original image. Look near the border, where distortion is easiest to see.

i

Lens Preview shows the effect in the viewport’s Rendered shading mode. Check the distortion again in your final render or composite.

05 / Photo & video

Floor, origin and real-world scale

The camera match tells you where things appear. Floor, origin and scale make that space useful for modelling, shadows and animation.

Set Floor#

WHERE Photo → Floor → Set Floor

Click the surface your object should rest on, such as a floor or tabletop. Perspectra sets that height to Z = 0 and displays the camera height. Reset restores the automatic floor estimate.

i

For a vase on a table, click the tabletop. Clicking the room floor sets a lower resting point.

Pick Floor and Set Origin#

WHERE Video → Floor and Scale

Click Pick Floor to set the surface your objects will stand on. Use Set Origin to choose where the scene coordinates start. If the ground still looks uneven against the footage, adjust Floor Height and the two Tilt controls.

Pick Floor and Set Origin controls
CONTROL WHAT IT DOES
Floor Height Move the floor up or down against the footage.
Tilt ↕ / Tilt ↔ Correct the floor’s forward/back and left/right tilt.
Reset Floor and Scale Return floor, origin and scale to their automatic alignment. Use when manual adjustments have become hard to evaluate.
i

If one click leaves the floor tilted, add Surface Trackers to several parts of the floor, then use Fit Floor.

Scale from a Known Size#

WHERE Photo → Floor / Video → Floor and Scale

Draw a line across something you’ve measured, such as a door or product box. Enter its real length and apply the scale. Camera height and the distances between objects change together.

  1. Choose Scale from a Known Size and mark the two ends of the measurement.
  2. Check the displayed Current length, enter the Real size in the scene’s units, then click Apply Scale.
  3. Check another visible dimension if possible. Cancel drops the measurement without applying it.
i

Measure between points whose depth is clear in the photo. A known length sets the scale, but distances elsewhere still depend on the estimated depth.

Scale from a Person#

WHERE Video → Floor and Scale

When you have no measured object, place the reference figure beside a standing person in the shot. Set its Height, then adjust Scene scale until the two look the same height.

i

The default figure is 1.70 m. Use the person’s known height when available; crouching, perspective, shoes and uneven ground make a generic height only an approximation. This scale reference is separate from Tracking People.

06 / Video

Track a video camera

Perspectra combines image tracking with estimated scene depth to build an animated Blender camera. Work with a continuous shot and review the whole result before adding final assets.

Track Video#

WHERE Video → source field → Track Video

Choose a video or an image-sequence folder. You can also leave the source blank to use the clip in the Movie Clip Editor. Perspectra builds an animated camera, adds the footage as its background, matches the timing and resolution, and places the floor and scene points.

  1. Choose a source and start with Normal. Read any footage-check warnings.
  2. Click Track Video. Ignore People is enabled by default in the current build. Watch the progress bar and use Cancel if you need to stop.
  3. After the first track, use Preview Mask under Ignore People or a listed object to check its outline. Correct missed areas with that row’s Edit Mask, then re-track.
  4. Play through the entire shot with a Test Cube or floor grid. Inspect weak sections and repair them before placing finished objects.
i

A plausible camera path is not proof of a good match. The useful check is whether geometry stays attached to the same real surfaces over time.

Frame sampling and range#

WHERE Video → Track Every Frame / Advanced → Start and End

For a difficult shot, set Start and End around a short stretch first. End = 0 tracks to the end of the clip. Track Every Frame is off by default, so the tracker samples every second frame. Enable it for fast motion. Even a short clip can need overlapping batches at the selected sampling rate. See the six-second clip example under Worker Memory Budget. Normal may also compare a second solve with shorter windows against the footage. After a new track finishes, the sidebar shows elapsed time, worker CPU time and GPU time when available. CPU time accumulates across threads. When device timing is unavailable, the panel can show accelerated inference duration separately.

i

On skipped frames, Perspectra estimates the camera position from nearby frames. Play those stretches back to check fast motion. The quality preset doesn’t set a maximum clip length.

Auto, Tripod and Moving camera#

WHERE Video → Advanced → Camera

Leave this on Auto unless you know the camera moved differently from the estimate. Tripod holds the camera in one place and allows pan and tilt. Choose Moving if the camera itself changes position, as in a walking or dolly shot.

i

When a tripod camera pans, the view changes but the camera stays in one place. If a tripod shot drifts with Moving selected, switch to Tripod and track it again.

Track Relative to Object#

WHERE Perspectra sidebar → Video → Advanced → Track Relative to Object

This checkbox is on by default. In Auto camera mode, Perspectra checks eligible shots for two motions. For example, if you walk down the aisle of a moving bus, the seats can reveal how the camera moves inside the bus. Stationary features visible through the windows can reveal how the bus moves through the scene. When both motions are verified, Perspectra creates an animated parent for the bus’s motion and a child camera for the movement inside it.

To use the standard camera solve, clear the checkbox before clicking Track Video or Re-track. To evaluate an existing shot with object-relative tracking, enable the option and re-track. When both camera views are available, click Use Original Camera or Use Onboard Camera.

Fixed lens, Zoom and Zoom + move#

WHERE Video → Advanced → Zoom

Choose Fixed if the focal length stayed the same. For a lens zoom, use Zoom if the camera stayed in one place, or Zoom + move if it also changed position. Leave it on Auto if you’re unsure.

Fixed lens, Zoom and Zoom + move controls
CONTROL WHAT IT DOES
Zoom smoothness Higher values favour a smoother focal-length curve; lower values follow measured changes more closely. Shown for the relevant automatic or moving-zoom modes.
i

Changes from digital stabilisation or an animated crop can resemble zoom. Review framing across the shot instead of trusting a mode label alone.

Known lens, Find Lens and reset#

WHERE Video → Lens and Speed × before tracking, or below Re-track after tracking

Before the first track, enter a known lens in mm and set Speed × manually. Use 1 for normal playback or 0.5 for half-speed footage. The saved multiplier scales the camera’s travel distance when the tracking result is applied. After tracking, the FOV, mm, Speed × and Find Lens controls appear below Re-track. If you don’t know the lens, Find Lens estimates it using at least two track points. Reset returns to automatic lens selection.

  1. Use a known value if it matches the actual crop and camera mode of your footage. Otherwise, improve tracking evidence and use Find Lens.
  2. Click Re-track to apply a changed lens to the camera solve.
  3. Check a nearby object and a distant one, both in the centre and near the edge of the frame.
i

The video mm field is explicitly 35 mm equivalent. Typing a value does not immediately replace the existing track; the panel warns while a lens change is pending.

Re-track and reuse analysis#

WHERE Video → Re-track

Re-track updates the camera after you change the lens, camera motion or exclusion masks. Perspectra reuses cached analysis where it can. After a local mask edit, the main button may offer just the affected frames; the adjacent full re-track button processes the whole range.

i

Check the frame range on the button before starting. After a mask edit, you may only need to track those frames again.

07 / Photo & video

Check the match in 3D

Watch a corner of the test cube as the shot plays. It should stay on the same spot on the floor, even when the camera moves. A green quality strip alone won’t show you whether it does.

Footage check and Tracking Quality#

WHERE Video → clip information → Show Tracking Quality

Normal and Best check the footage automatically for conditions that could make the shot difficult. After tracking, scrub through the quality strip to find weak stretches. The panel tells you whether the current frame was tracked or interpolated from nearby frames.

i

Read the text as well as the colour. Review sudden changes, blur, occlusion and shot cuts in the actual footage. A good-looking status is not a substitute for a stable test object.

Test Cube#

WHERE Photo → Floor / Video → Check in 3D

Place a cube where a corner should touch the ground. In Video, adjust Size and Rotation, then play the clip. If the corner floats or slides across the floor, check the match before placing your final model.

i

A cube that stays fixed at one spot can still reveal errors elsewhere. Inspect more than one depth or area when the shot allows it.

Scene Points#

WHERE Video → Check in 3D → Scene Points

Show scene points to see which parts of the background the camera track picked up. Lower Max Point Error to hide less reliable points, or increase Point size if the dots are hard to see.

i

Max Point Error only changes which points you see. Hiding a point here doesn’t remove it from the camera fit.

Show Floor Grid#

WHERE Video → Check in 3D → Show Floor Grid

Overlay the grid to check a larger patch of ground than a test cube covers. Adjust the spacing to suit the shot. Hide Grid Behind Objects uses estimated depth to hide grid lines where something stands in front of them.

i

Depth-based occlusion is an estimate. If the grid appears oddly clipped around objects, disable Hide Grid Behind Objects while checking the floor itself.

08 / Video

Fix a difficult track

Scrub to the first frame where the track slips. Fix the point, edge or surface that lost its place, then solve the camera again. Leave smoothing until the camera lines up.

Refine Here#

WHERE Video → Fix Tracking → Refine Here

If the camera drifts for a few frames, move to the middle of that stretch and run Refine Here. The ± Frames setting controls how far Perspectra tracks on either side. Check the displayed range before you start.

  1. Move to the middle of the problem span.
  2. Set ± Frames wide enough to include stable footage on both sides.
  3. Run Refine Here, then compare the repaired span and its boundaries.

Bridge Frames From Here#

WHERE Video → Fix Tracking

Pick a frame before the track was lost and another where the same background is visible again. Perspectra looks for details it can match across the gap. You can review or remove a saved bridge, or run the search again.

Bridge or refine?

Use Refine Here if the detail stays visible but the track drifts. Try a bridge if a bus hides the background for several frames and the same wall reappears after it passes.

  1. Go to a useful frame near one side of the loss and click Bridge Frames From Here.
  2. Scrub to the other side and click Bridge [start–end].
  3. Review the recovered points and camera continuity. Use Cancel to abandon a pending span, or remove a saved bridge if its connection is wrong.
i

Bridge one continuous scene. Do not try to connect unrelated shots across an edit, or use a moving subject as the stationary reference.

Add Track Point#

WHERE Video → Fix Tracking → Track Points

Pick a fixed detail you can recognise across frames, such as the corner of a window. Position the preview on that detail, then click Track It. A point is particularly useful in an area with few automatic tracks.

  1. Click Add Track Point and place it on a sharp stationary detail.
  2. Check the candidate, then choose Track It.
  3. Inspect its path across frames. Spread points over the image and use different depths where possible.
  4. Use the eye for display, the checkboxes to include or exclude points, and X to remove a point. Show List refreshes the list when offered.
i

Spread points across fixed parts of the scene. A few clear corners on different buildings are more useful than a cluster on leaves, shadows or reflections.

Merge Points and duplicate suggestions#

WHERE Video → Fix Tracking → Track Points

If Perspectra loses a feature and picks it up again as a new point, you can join the two tracks. Select the point to keep first, select the others, then confirm. For automatic suggestions, choose Merge or Keep Separate.

i

Never merge merely nearby features. A false merge ties different 3D locations together and can distort the camera. Keep Separate dismisses an incorrect suggestion without changing either track.

Add Track Edge#

WHERE Video → Fix Tracking → Track Edges

Track a straight edge when you can follow a wall seam or window frame more easily than a single dot. The camera fit uses the line. From the edge list you can jump to it, track it again, disable or remove it, or hide its overlay.

i

Pick an edge you can recognise throughout the shot, such as the side of a pillar. Reflections and the outline of a passing car move even when the camera holds still. After correcting an edge, track it again before solving the camera.

Add Surface Tracker#

WHERE Video → Fix Tracking → Track Surfaces

Pick three spots on the same flat surface, such as a tabletop. Check the grid, then click Confirm Surface. For a patch of ground, enable Floor so the solve keeps it level and uses it to help set camera height.

  1. Pick three spots spread across the same flat, rigid surface. They should form a triangle rather than a straight line.
  2. Use Grid and Spacing to inspect the surface. Adjust Height and Tilt if needed.
  3. Enable Floor only for actual floor/support planes, then click Confirm Surface or press Enter.
  4. Use Preview Surface Tracking to inspect the tracked planes through the shot.
i

Keep all three spots on the surface you want to track. Two on a table and one on the wall behind it will give the grid the wrong tilt.

Fit Floor to Surfaces#

WHERE Video → Fix Tracking → Track Surfaces

Use several floor trackers to correct the ground height or tilt. Perspectra previews the plane and shows which trackers agree with it and which it left out. Check the preview before clicking Apply Floor.

i

Check which trackers were used before applying the floor. Leave out any on a stair tread, raised platform or tabletop above floor level.

Clean Up Points, Edges and Surfaces#

WHERE Video → Fix Tracking → the matching tracking-data box

Run the cleanup for the kind of track that’s slipping. Each tool checks its own tracks for drift or conflicting positions. Point cleanup can also find a lost stretch again or disable a weak point. The status tells you what changed.

i

Clean Up can keep a point that stays on the right feature even if the camera projects it slightly off target. If it still looks wrong, check the lens and the feature it follows before running cleanup again.

Solve Camera#

WHERE Video → Fix Tracking → Solve Camera

After adding or correcting tracks, run Solve Camera to fit the camera to the enabled points, edges and surfaces. You can cancel while it runs. If a reset control appears, it removes this extra fit.

i

Check for points that jump to another feature before solving. A bad track can pull the camera away from the background. Solve Camera appears once there’s enough usable tracking data.

Match Mesh to Footage and pins#

WHERE Video → Fix Tracking → Adjust Manually

Choose a rigid mesh in the scene and drag its projected points onto the matching corners in the footage. The camera moves to fit. Add a pin to keep the correction on this frame and let it fade into the frames around it.

Match Mesh to Footage and pins controls
CONTROL WHAT IT DOES
Keep Camera Height Allow turning and sliding while maintaining height. Useful when the floor is already correct.
Done Matching Finish the active matching tool.
Pin checkbox / X Disable a correction temporarily or remove it.
Fade (frames) Control how far the local correction spreads into neighbouring frames. Inspect the transitions on both sides.
i

Check the block’s size and position first. If it’s too large or too far away, matching its corners can move the camera to the wrong place. Pins work best for small corrections after the lens and scene are lined up.

Camera Smoothing#

WHERE Video → Fix Tracking → below Solve Camera

If the camera lines up but jitters on playback, start with a little smoothing. Unlink Position and Rotation if only one needs adjusting. Set either to zero to use the original motion for that component.

i

Smoothing affects the camera over the clip, not just one pin. Too much can make geometry slide during real motion or soften intentional bumps. It cannot repair a wrong lens or an incorrect track.

09 / Video

Exclude moving subjects

Use Exclude from Camera Tracking to keep moving subjects out of the camera solve. Ignore People and each object you click have their own preview and edits. The solver combines their masks, so a pixel covered by two masks stays excluded when you erase it from just one.

Ignore People#

WHERE Video → Exclude from Camera Tracking

Ignore People is on by default and targets people. For a passing car or another moving object, use Ignore Object. If the detector briefly loses a hand or person, Perspectra follows a previously confirmed outline while its motion and appearance still match the footage.

i

Scrub the clip with the people preview on. If a thin strip of the silhouette falls outside the red overlay, increase Padding. The default padding expands the people outline by 1.5% of the frame’s longer side.

Ignore Object#

WHERE Video → Exclude from Camera Tracking → Ignore Object

Click Ignore Object, then click the subject in the footage on a frame where its outline is clear. Each pick adds a numbered row with the frame you clicked. If the outline detector misses the object, Perspectra follows its last reliable outline while the footage still supports it. Check the listed frame ranges and scrub across any occlusion.

i

Use the circular arrow (Refresh Object Mask) beside the object to follow it again from its original click and keep its painted edits. Use this for an object saved with an earlier version. The × beside the object removes it from the exclusion list.

Preview Mask and Edit Mask#

WHERE Video → Exclude from Camera Tracking → Ignore People or a numbered object

  1. In camera view, click Preview Mask under the subject you want to check. Red shows that subject’s exclusion on the current frame. Click another row’s preview to switch, or click the active preview again to hide it.
  2. Scrub to the problem frame and click Edit Mask in the same row. Drag with Brush to add a missed area or Ctrl-drag to erase. Use Polyline for a straight-edged area or Smart to guide the outline with clicks.
  3. Set Apply to ± Frames to the number of frames on either side that should receive the correction. Use 0 for a single frame. Choose Apply Mask to keep the edits or Discard Changes to undo this editing session.
  4. Check the preview on nearby frames. Re-track the range or whole clip indicated by Mask changes pending to use the edits in the camera solve.
i

In the edited-frame summary, × clears the current frame’s edits and the trash icon clears all edits for that mask. Older projects may also show Previous combined edits for corrections made before people and objects had separate masks.

10 / Scene objects

Build objects from the reference

Use simple geometry for blocking and contact checks, or try a depth-based mesh when the visible shape matters. Confirmed objects are starting points you can continue editing in Blender.

Pick Object and Add to Scene#

WHERE Photo or Video → 3D Objects from the Photo / Footage

Click an object in the image to preview its mask and a fitted shape. Adjust the outline and shape, then click Add to Scene to keep it or Discard Object to start again. A simple proxy is often enough for a shadow or contact surface.

  1. Match the camera and floor first, then choose Pick Object in Photo or Pick Object in Footage.
  2. Click inside the subject. In Photo mode, Standard and Pro 0.1.2 use the surrounding background to refine the outline and use the connected regions you picked for the fit. Shift-click a detached part to include it. Ctrl-click an unwanted area to exclude it.
  3. Inspect the chosen shape, outline and depth.
  4. Correct the mask if needed, then use Add to Scene or Discard Object.
i

A single photo shows only one side of the object. Check the dimensions against a known measurement and inspect the back of the mesh before using it in another view.

Box, Cylinder, Ball and Plane#

WHERE Object preview → shape buttons

Pick the simplest shape that fits the job. A box works for blocking out a cabinet; a plane is enough if all you need is a surface to catch its shadow.

Box, Cylinder, Ball and Plane controls
CONTROL WHAT IT DOES
Box Packages, cabinets, crates and other rigid rectangular forms. Also useful as the reference for Match Mesh to Footage.
Cylinder Cans, tubes, columns and roughly cylindrical bodies.
Ball Balls and approximately spherical forms.
Plane Flat surfaces, panels or simple contact and projection geometry.

Photo Matching#

WHERE 3D Viewport sidebar → Perspectra → Photo → Photo Matching

Available in Standard and Pro from 0.1.2. After estimating the camera and choosing Add to Scene, select the mesh in Object Mode and look through the matched camera. For a lens-distorted photo, switch the background to Undistorted.

  • Fit Primitive to Image — Drag a corner or edge pin onto the corresponding feature in the photo. One pin positions the mesh at its estimated depth. Add a second to adjust size and a third on another face to help set the heading.
  • Fit Image Camera to 3D — Use this when the mesh already has the right placement and dimensions. Drag its pins onto matching features in the photo to adjust the camera pose. The adjustment affects the projection of the whole scene.
  • Fit Cylinder Rims — Drag the left end, front-arc midpoint and right end of each rim onto the corresponding image features. Use both rims to fit the cylinder’s height and diameter.

Release inside the photo to apply each pin. Releasing outside the photo discards that drag. Press Enter to keep the fit or Esc to restore the starting transform.

Real: Free form and Smooth round#

WHERE Full edition → Photo → Real / Video → Mesh

Perspectra turns the masked area into a mesh and uses the reference image as its texture. Choose how to build the surface based on the object’s outline.

Choosing the surface

Use Free form for an irregular surface where the visible depth matters. For a bottle, can or jar, Smooth round builds a surface around an axis from its profile.

Real: Free form and Smooth round controls
CONTROL WHAT IT DOES
Faces Sets the target face count, from 200 to 50,000. A higher count can show finer surface detail, but it takes more processing and can’t reveal parts hidden in the photo.
Hidden side: Auto Let Perspectra choose how to build the hidden side based on the shape it fitted.
Hidden side: Off Close the back with the fitted shape.
Hidden side: Mirror Mirror the visible half onto the hidden side. This works best when both halves have the same shape.
Hidden side: Turn Rotate the visible surface around a vertical axis, as you would for a bottle or a vase.
i

The texture includes shadows and highlights from the photo. They’ll still be there if you relight the mesh in Blender. Perspectra also has to estimate the shape and texture on the hidden side.

Edit Object Mask#

WHERE Object preview → Edit Object Mask

If the fit misses a handle or includes part of the background, fix the outline first. Brush works for small touch-ups. Polyline lets you place the boundary vertex by vertex. With Smart, mark areas to include or exclude.

Edit Object Mask controls
CONTROL WHAT IT DOES
Brush Paint the object region; Ctrl erases. Use the wheel to change brush size where the active tool supports it.
Polyline Outline clear geometric boundaries with points; follow the tool’s confirm hint to finish.
Smart Mark a few areas to keep or leave out, then let Smart update the outline.
Apply Mask / Discard Mask Changes Commit the edited outline and rebuild the preview, or revert the active edit.

Build an object across a clip#

WHERE Video → 3D Objects from the Footage

In Standard, pick a primitive, then choose Add to Scene for a static placement. For a moving primitive, enable Animate from Footage, click Use This Object and add it when tracking finishes.

In the full edition, choose a primitive or Mesh before picking the object. Use This Object follows the outline through the shot. Review the masks, fix any that slip, then click Confirm Masks before building the shape.

  1. Pick the object on a clear frame. At mask confirmation, leave Object Is Stationary enabled for a fixed reference, or choose Animate from Footage to track a moving object. The choices are mutually exclusive. Click Use This Object. Use Pick Again if the identity is wrong.
  2. Scrub the clip. Use Edit Mask on This Frame where needed.
  3. Enable Carry Edits to Nearby Frames and set ± only if the nearby motion supports propagation; inspect those frames too.
  4. Choose Confirm Masks, inspect the fitted shape, then Add to Scene.
i

For a moving object, Perspectra follows visible feature points inside the reviewed mask and fits the mesh’s position and rotation. Check the turn on frames where texture disappears or another object crosses in front.

Review and add the fitted object#

WHERE Video → 3D Objects from the Footage → object preview

Inspect the fitted shape before choosing Add to Scene. In the full edition, use Show Mask or Edit Object Mask in the preview. To keep a box outline as a camera exclusion, choose Create Clip Ignore Mask. Its entry can then be edited or removed in the exclusion list.

Add to Scene finishes the picking session. Select the deployed mesh in Blender to edit it. If you chose Animate from Footage, its position and rotation are editable keyframes.

Place a Marker or the selected object#

WHERE Video → 3D Objects from the Footage → Marker

Click a spot in the footage to place a reference marker there for later modelling. If you have an eligible scene object selected, the tool can place that object instead. Check the button label before clicking.

i

Check contact and scale across the shot after placement. A clicked depth location is an estimate and may need a manual adjustment in Blender.

11 / People & animation

Track a person’s movement

Match the camera and set the floor first so the animated character stands in the right place. This chapter covers editions that include Tracking People.

Pick Person#

WHERE Tracking People → Pick Person

In a video, pick the person whose movement you want to use for a character. If you’re working from a still photo, the full build can fit a character to the pose using the object/person tools.

  1. Match the camera, set the floor and check the scene scale.
  2. Find a frame where the person is easy to see. Choose Pick Person and click them.
  3. Check the highlighted outline, choose the model and refinements, then click Confirm. The progress bar and cancel control appear inside Tracking People. Use Reject to pick again.
  4. Play the clip and watch the character’s feet. Do they touch down on the same frames as the performer’s feet, even after the performer steps out from behind something?
i

You can use Ignore People and Tracking People on the same shot. Ignore People keeps a walking performer from pulling the camera track off course. Tracking People uses that performer’s movement to animate a character.

Adjust Height and Build#

WHERE Tracking People → tracked person

Open the card named for the scene object, such as Perspectra_Person_2. Height and Build show the values used for that fit. Enter a known height or adjust Build if the figure looks too broad or narrow. ANNY fits its own body shape and shows Gender in place of the Build control.

You can change several fields together. Apply Changes updates this person using their saved tracking. Revert Changes restores the last applied settings and discards any staged pose edits.

Bones, Mixamo, ANNY and Custom#

WHERE Tracking People → Pick Person → highlighted outline → Default Model

Choose Bones for the animated skeleton alone, Mixamo for the bundled character, or ANNY to fit a body to the performer. With ANNY, choose the gender setting before confirming.

Choose Custom to use your own rig, then select its Target Armature. For an already tracked person, use the Model selector on their card and click Apply Changes.

Join or remove a tracked person#

WHERE Tracking People → tracked person’s header

If two tracks belong to the same performer, use the link icon for Same Person As. Use the × on a person’s card to remove that character. If the card reports a timing mismatch, use Apply Changes to restore the animation timing.

Choose tracking refinements#

WHERE Tracking People → highlighted person → before Confirm

Refine with GEM-X is selected by default and runs during the person track when the required models are available. Clear it to skip that refinement.

Track Fingers and Toes (Beta) is off by default. Enable it to track the digits and fit visible finger motion. With it off, the digits follow the hands and feet. Refine Foot Rotation (Experimental) and Refine Wrist Depth (Beta) can be selected independently.

Reconstruct Hidden Body Motion (Beta)#

WHERE Tracking People → highlighted person → before Confirm

Enable Reconstruct Hidden Body Motion (Beta) to let MotionBricks estimate movement while part of the performer is hidden. Set the video’s Speed × to match the footage before tracking.

When the result contains MotionBricks contacts, the person’s card shows controls to inspect and edit them. Scrub across the first visible frame after an occlusion to check where a foot lands or a hand meets a prop.

12 / People & animation

Edit poses and retarget motion

Adjust a hand, foot or other joint where the pose doesn’t match the footage. The bones keep their lengths as you edit. Once the motion looks right, you can transfer it to another rig.

Edit Pose Here#

WHERE Tracking People → person → Edit Pose Here

Pause on the frame you want to fix. Select a joint or bone, then drag it or press G to move it. Press R to rotate. Choose Stage Pose Edit to queue the correction. On the person’s card, Apply Changes commits the draft and Revert Changes discards it.

Edit Pose Here controls
CONTROL WHAT IT DOES
Auto selection Prefer a joint near its ring; otherwise pick the bone under the pointer.
Joint Pick joint endpoints and adjust connected bones.
Bone Pick a bone for rotation or chain movement.
Move parents: Through body Allow the chain to reach through the spine and pelvis when the nearer joints reach their limits.
Move parents: Limb only Keep the arm anchored at its shoulder or leg at its hip.
Stage Pose Edit / Cancel Stage the correction for review or discard the current edit.
i

Stay on the frame where editing began. If you scrub away, return to that frame to stage the edit, or Cancel and start an edit on the new frame. Bone lengths stay fixed; this is not a body-resizing tool.

Joint rings, tracked dots and the foot fan#

WHERE Viewport while Edit Pose Here is active

The rings are joints you can edit; the blue and orange dots are tracked positions. To check a flipped foot, look at the fan: blue is the top, orange is the underside, and the arrow points away from the sole. The heel controls move with the foot.

i

The foot fan is an orientation guide tied to the character. It is not a traced shoe silhouette or proof that the foot matches the footage.

Blend Window, Transition and motion paths#

WHERE Edit Pose Here → correction settings

If a corrected hand jumps on the next frame, increase Blend Window to let the edit fade across neighbouring frames. Smooth eases the transition; Linear fades at a constant rate. Turn on Show Before / After Paths to see where the hand will travel before you keep the edit.

Blend Window, Transition and motion paths controls
CONTROL WHAT IT DOES
Blend Window Zero confines the correction to its frame; a larger window spreads it further. The current controls allow up to 240 frames each side.
Before / After Paths Grey shows the original path; cyan shows the proposed path. Dots mark past frames; brighter lines indicate future frames.
Clear Pose Fix Remove the correction on the current frame, or use the all-edits control to remove the person’s saved pose fixes.
i

After changing the blend, play across nearby edits. Check that a planted foot stays on the ground and a hand still meets the object it touches.

Use a custom skeleton#

WHERE Tracking People → Default Model or tracked person → Model

To trace onto your rig, choose Custom and select the Target Armature while reviewing the highlighted person. Click Map Target Bones and inspect Edit Bone Mapping before confirming the trace.

For a saved track, choose Custom on the person’s card, select the target and click Apply Changes. Play through a planted foot or a hand contact to check how the motion fits the target’s proportions.

13 / Video

Saved data and cache cleanup

A saved .blend refers to external footage and analysis files. Keep the files needed to reopen a track, and free reusable analysis when you need disk space.

Free Cache and Relink Track Result#

WHERE Video → cache status / missing track-result notice

Free Cache clears reusable analysis for this clip and keeps its tracking result. If a project has moved and Blender can’t find the saved result, use Relink Track Result to reconnect it to an available result for the same clip.

Free Cache and Relink Track Result controls
CONTROL WHAT IT DOES
Cache folder Choose a persistent writable location in Preferences. Existing scenes remember where their tracking data was stored.
Free Cache Recover disk space. Future operations may need to recompute the removed heavy analysis.
Relink Track Result Use the newest available saved result for the same clip when the previous result is missing.
i

When moving or archiving a project, keep the footage, .blend and tracking results together. Free Cache removes reusable analysis and leaves the finished scene in place.

14 / Reference

Workflow recipes

Each example starts with a shot and lists the steps to take in Blender.

01

Insert a product into a image

Estimate Camera → correct Guide Lines → Set Floor → Scale from a Known Size → Test Cube → place or model the asset.

Open the guide ↗
02

Add CG to a moving shot

Track Video → inspect Tracking Quality → check a cube and grid → repair weak spans → Solve Camera → place the asset.

Open the guide ↗
03

Repair one short tracking failure

Scrub to where the track slips, check the masks, then run Refine Here. If something blocks the view and the same background reappears, try bridging the frames on either side of the gap.

Open the guide ↗
04

Stop a passing person from pulling the camera

Enable Ignore People and scrub with its Preview Mask on. Adjust Padding or use Edit Mask where the outline misses the person. Re-track and check that the background stays fixed.

Open the guide ↗
05

Recreate an object from the image

Match the camera and scale → Pick Object → correct the mask → choose a primitive, Real (photo) or Mesh (video) → inspect multiple views when available → Add to Scene.

Open the guide ↗
06

Put an animated character in the performer’s place

Match the camera and floor, then use Pick Person. Check the character’s size and play through any parts where the performer is hidden. Fix poses with Edit Pose Here, blend the edits into nearby frames, then transfer the motion to your rig.

Open the guide ↗

15 / Reference

Keyboard & mouse

These shortcuts work while the tool in the first column is active. Follow the hints shown in the viewport if they differ.

Keyboard and mouse controls
CONTEXT INPUT ACTION
Interface N Open or close the 3D Viewport sidebar; choose Perspectra.
Guide Lines Drag a handle Move a vanishing-line endpoint or, on a distorted original photo, a lens-bend middle handle.
Guide Lines Hold Tab Show the ground grid and horizon while checking the guides.
Guide Lines Enter / C Confirm the active guide-line edit.
Guide Lines Esc / right-click Cancel the active guide-line edit.
Object picking Shift-click / Ctrl-click Add a part to / remove a part from the object selection.
Mask brush Ctrl Erase while painting; follow the active tool’s hints.
Mask brush Mouse wheel Adjust brush size in the mask painting tools that expose this shortcut.
Mask editing Enter / Esc Finish or cancel where supported; the Apply / Discard buttons make the action explicit.
Surface Tracker Enter Confirm the three-point surface.
Pose editing G / drag Move the selected joint or bone control with the supported chain behaviour.
Pose editing R Rotate the selected pose control.

16 / Reference

Troubleshooting

Start with the symptom you can see. Change one thing, then check the result against the footage.

Perspectra is missing from the sidebar.+

Check that the add-on is enabled and you are in the 3D Viewport. Press N and look for the Perspectra tab. If registration failed, check Blender’s console and the add-on’s installation status. People controls require an edition that includes them.

The estimate or track will not start.+

Read the missing-package or model notice. Open add-on preferences, install the required files for the selected mode, and run Test Installed Models. Check that the source and cache folder are readable/writable. Restart Blender if the installer reports a pending package replacement.

The lens or horizon is uncertain.+

In Photo, place Guide Lines along edges you know are straight, such as door frames. A head-on view may give few clues about the lens. In Video, enter a known horizontal FOV or 35 mm-equivalent focal length, or try Find Lens. Re-track after changing the lens.

The camera fits the centre but not the edges.+

Check lens distortion, crop and perspective mode. In Photo compare Original photo with Undistorted, and correct lens bend only using real straight edges. In Video verify the lens and zoom mode. A rolling-shutter or stabilisation warp may not fit one simple camera/lens model.

My cube slides even though the quality strip looks good.+

Watch a fixed point beside the cube as the clip plays. Check the camera type, lens and scale. If a marker slips, correct it and add points, an edge or a surface elsewhere in the scene, then run Solve Camera. Try reducing smoothing if the camera lags behind a real movement.

Everything floats or is the wrong size.+

Separate floor height from scale. Set or pick the correct support surface first, then use a known size. If the floor tilts, use several floor Surface Trackers and inspect the fitted plane. A person-size reference gives only an approximate scale unless their height is known.

A moving person or car seems to drag the camera.+

For a person, enable Ignore People. For a car, click Ignore Object and pick the car. Use Preview Mask in the corresponding row to find where the outline slips. Correct it with that row’s Edit Mask, then re-track. Leave stationary background visible for the solver.

Clean Up keeps some imperfect-looking points.+

A point can follow the right corner even if the estimated camera puts it a few pixels away. Scrub through the shot: if the point stays on the corner, check the lens; if it jumps to a different detail, disable or correct that track before solving again.

The reconstructed mesh has a distorted back or painted shadows.+

The photo doesn’t show the back of the object, and its shadows are part of the texture. Check the mask and any other views in the clip. For a bottle or jar, try Smooth round. For a box, a simple primitive may give a cleaner result. You can edit the mesh and material in Blender afterwards.

The same performer appears twice, or the animation is out of sync.+

If two tracks follow the same performer, join them with Same Person As. If the movement is out of sync, check the frame rate, tracking range and any gaps. Use Apply Changes on the person’s card when the panel flags a timing mismatch, then review the animation before editing poses.

Stage Pose Edit is unavailable after I scrub the timeline.+

An edit belongs to the frame where it started. Return to that frame to stage it, or Cancel and start Edit Pose Here on the new frame. Review the Before / After paths when changing the correction window.

Retargeting does not drive my custom rig correctly.+

Inspect Bone Mapping and the reference pose. The current retargeter expects compatible FK bones or controls and cannot automatically resolve every constrained IK rig. Prepare a suitable target or transfer the resulting action through your rig’s own animation workflow.

A run stopped after reaching the worker memory budget.+

During a full video track, let automatic batch retries finish. A run can still stop if a model, the smallest tracking batch or final assembly needs more memory than the budget allows. Let other Perspectra jobs finish before retrying. If your computer has RAM to spare, raise Worker Memory Budget for the next run. A lighter preset can reduce a model’s requirements, and a shorter frame range can reduce assembly memory.

A saved project cannot find its tracking result.+

Check that the external media and cache/result files still exist. Use Relink Track Result if Perspectra offers another result for the same clip. Otherwise restore the missing files from your project backup or re-track the source.

17 / Reference

A few useful terms

FOV
Field of view: the angle covered by the image. Perspectra’s lens controls use horizontal FOV.
Vanishing point
Where projections of parallel 3D lines meet in the image.
Lens shift
An offset of the framing without tilting the camera; useful for keeping verticals parallel.
Parallax
Near and far objects moving differently in the image as the camera translates.
Reprojection error
The image-space distance between an observed feature and its predicted position, usually expressed in pixels.
Depth / metric scale
Depth estimates distances into the scene. Metric scale relates the reconstructed scene to real-world units; verify it with a known measurement.
Mask
An area marked in an image. A camera mask marks what tracking should ignore; an object mask outlines the part you want to turn into a mesh.
Pin
A stored local camera correction on a frame, with a configurable fade into neighbouring frames.
FK / IK
Forward kinematics rotates bones down a hierarchy. Inverse kinematics moves a target and adjusts a chain to reach it.
Retargeting
Transferring motion between skeletons while respecting their different structures and proportions.
